chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sulaym al-Farrāʾ, who said:

I asked him about a man who is the muʾadhdhin of a people and their Imam, and he is on the road to Makkah or elsewhere, so he leads them in the ʿasr prayer in its time. Then a man enters who does not know and thinks that it is the first prayer; would it suffice for him if it is actually the ʿasr prayer? He said: No.

key_terms.أَفَيُجْزِيهِ: would it be sufficient or valid for him
key_terms.الْأُولَى: the first prayer, here meaning al-ẓuhr
key_terms.مُؤَذِّنَ: the one who gives the call to prayer

ai.seo_question: Does joining ʿasr prayer while thinking it is ẓuhr count as valid?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning one who joins a congregational ʿasr prayer while assuming it is the first prayer, meaning al-ẓuhr. The Imam عليه السلام rules that it does not suffice, indicating the importance of specifying the correct prayer in such a situation.
